sanskrit: tato rāvaṇanītāyāḥ sītāyāḥ śatrukarśanaḥ iyeṣa padam anveṣṭuṃ cāraṇācarite pathi
english: Then he, the crusher of foes, resolved to seek the track of Sītā who had been carried off by Rāvaṇa, on the path frequented by the Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: atha vaidūryavarṇeṣu śādvaleṣu mahābalaḥ dhīraḥ salilakalpeṣu vicacāra yathāsukham
english: Then the mighty, steadfast one roamed at ease over the verdant meadows colored like vaidūrya gems, which were as level as water.

sanskrit: dvijān vitrāsayan dhīmān urasā pādapān haran mṛgāṃś ca subahūn nighnan pravṛddha iva kesarī
english: Terrifying the birds, smashing trees with his chest, slaying many deer — he was like a fully grown lion.

sanskrit: nīlalohitamāñjiṣṭhapadmavarṇaiḥ sitāsitaiḥ svabhāvavihitaiś citrair dhātubhiḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: The mountain was adorned with variegated mineral ores of their natural hues — blue, red, crimson, lotus-pink, white, and black.

sanskrit: kāmarūpibhir āviṣṭam abhīkṣṇaṃ saparicchadaiḥ yakṣakiṃnaragandharvair devakalpaiś ca pannagaiḥ
english: It was thronged constantly, along with their retinues, by Yakṣas, Kiṃnaras, Gandharvas, and serpent-beings resembling gods, all assuming forms at will.

sanskrit: sa tasya girivaryasya tale nāgavarāyute tiṣṭhan kapivaras tatra hrade nāga ivābabhau
english: Standing at the foot of that foremost mountain, surrounded by lordly elephants, the best of monkeys shone there like an elephant in a lake.

sanskrit: sa sūryāya mahendrāya pavanāya svayambhuve bhūtebhyaś cāñjaliṃ kṛtvā cakāra gamane matim
english: Making añjali to Sūrya, to Mahendra, to Pavana, to Svayambhū, and to all beings, he made up his mind to depart.

sanskrit: añjaliṃ prāṅmukhaḥ kurvan pavanāyātmayonaye tato hi vavṛdhe gantuṃ dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Facing east, making añjali to Pavana, his own progenitor, he then grew in order to proceed south — the capable one toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: plavaṃgapravarair dṛṣṭaḥ plavane kṛtaniścayaḥ vavṛdhe rāmavṛddhyarthaṃ samudra iva parvasu
english: Seen by the foremost of leaping monkeys, resolved upon the crossing, he expanded for the benefit of Rāma's cause, as the ocean swells at the full moon.

sanskrit: niṣpramāṇa śarīraḥ saṃl lilaṅghayiṣur arṇavam bāhubhyāṃ pīḍayām āsa caraṇābhyāṃ ca parvatam
english: His body boundless, intent on leaping across the ocean, he pressed the mountain down with his arms and with his feet.

sanskrit: sa cacālācalāś cāru muhūrtaṃ kapipīḍitaḥ tarūṇāṃ puṣpitāgrāṇāṃ sarvaṃ puṣpam aśātayat
english: The lovely mountain, pressed by the monkey, trembled for a moment and shook all the blossoms from the flowering treetops.

sanskrit: tena pādapamuktena puṣpaugheṇa sugandhinā sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaḥ śailo babhau puṣpamayo yathā
english: Covered on all sides by that fragrant flood of flowers shed by the trees, the mountain shone as though it were made entirely of blossoms.

sanskrit: tena cottamavīryeṇa pīḍyamānaḥ sa parvataḥ salilaṃ saṃprasusrāva madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ
english: Pressed by that one of supreme valor, the mountain oozed forth water, like an elephant in rut exuding ichor.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānas tu balinā mahendras tena parvataḥ rītir nirvartayām āsa kāñcanāñjanarājatīḥ mumoca ca śilāḥ śailo viśālāḥ samanaḥśilāḥ
english: Pressed by that mighty one, mount Mahendra gave forth streams of gold, antimony, and silver, and the mountain discharged great slabs of rock along with slabs of soapstone.

sanskrit: giriṇā pīḍyamānena pīḍyamānāni sarvaśaḥ guhāviṣṭāni bhūtāni vinedur vikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ
english: As the mountain was compressed, the creatures dwelling in its caves, pressed on all sides, cried out with strange and terrible sounds.

sanskrit: sa mahāsattvasaṃnādaḥ śailapīḍānimittajaḥ pṛthivīṃ pūrayām āsa diśaś copavanāni ca
english: That great tumult of beings, arising from the mountain's compression, filled the earth and the directions and the groves on every side.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ pṛthubhiḥ sarpā vyaktasvastikalakṣaṇaiḥ vamantaḥ pāvakaṃ ghoraṃ dadaṃśur daśanaiḥ śilāḥ
english: Serpents with wide, clearly marked svastika-signs on their heads, vomiting terrible fire, bit the rocks with their fangs.

sanskrit: tās tadā saviṣair daṣṭāḥ kupitais tair mahāśilāḥ jajvaluḥ pāvakoddīptā vibhiduś ca sahasradhā
english: Those great slabs of rock, bitten by the enraged, venomous serpents, blazed up kindled with fire and split into thousands of fragments.

sanskrit: yāni cauṣadhajālāni tasmiñ jātāni parvate viṣaghnāny api nāgānāṃ na śekuḥ śamituṃ viṣam
english: Even the masses of herbs born on that mountain, though antidotes to serpent-venom, could not quell the poison of those Nāgas.

sanskrit: bhidyate 'yaṃ girir bhūtair iti matvā tapasvinaḥ trastā vidyādharās tasmād utpetuḥ strīgaṇaiḥ saha
english: Thinking "the mountain is being shattered by these beings," the ascetic Vidyādharas, frightened, flew up from it together with their bands of women.

sanskrit: pānabhūmigataṃ hitvā haimam āsanabhājanam pātrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi karakāṃś ca hiraṇmayān
english: Abandoning the golden vessels and seats left behind on the drinking grounds, the precious drinking cups, and the golden water-pots,

sanskrit: lehyān uccāvacān bhakṣyān māṃsāni vividhāni ca ārṣabhāṇi ca carmāṇi khaḍgāṃś ca kanakatsarūn
english: leaving behind lickable and various edible delicacies, different kinds of meats, bull-hides, and swords with golden hilts,

sanskrit: kṛtakaṇṭhaguṇāḥ kṣībā raktamālyānulepanāḥ raktākṣāḥ puṣkarākṣāś ca gaganaṃ pratipedire
english: adorned with garlands around their necks, intoxicated, wearing red garlands and unguents, with red eyes and lotus eyes, they took to the sky.

sanskrit: hāranūpurakeyūra pārihārya dharāḥ striyaḥ vismitāḥ sasmitās tasthur ākāśe ramaṇaiḥ saha
english: The women, wearing necklaces, anklets, armlets, and ornaments, astonished and smiling, stood in the sky together with their lovers.

sanskrit: darśayanto mahāvidyāṃ vidyādharamaharṣayaḥ sahitās tasthur ākāśe vīkṣāṃ cakruś ca parvatam
english: The Vidyādharas and great sages, displaying their great powers, stood together in the sky and gazed upon the mountain.

sanskrit: śuśruvuś ca tadā śabdam ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām cāraṇānāṃ ca siddhānāṃ sthitānāṃ vimale 'mbare
english: They also heard the words of the self-perfected sages, of the Cāraṇas, and of the Siddhas who stood in the clear sky.

sanskrit: eṣa parvatasaṃkāśo hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ titīrṣati mahāvegaṃ samudraṃ makarālayam
english: "This is Hanūmān, son of Māruta, mountain-like, who wishes to leap across the mighty, swift ocean, the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: rāmārthaṃ vānarārthaṃ ca cikīrṣan karma duṣkaram samudrasya paraṃ pāraṃ duṣprāpaṃ prāptum icchati
english: Wishing to accomplish a most difficult deed for the sake of Rāma and the monkeys, he desires to reach the far shore of the ocean — a shore most difficult to reach."

sanskrit: dudhuve ca sa romāṇi cakampe cācalopamaḥ nanāda ca mahānādaṃ sumahān iva toyadaḥ
english: He shook his body hair, and trembled though mountain-like, and let out a great roar like a vast thundercloud.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyāc ca vṛttaṃ ca lāṅgūlaṃ romabhiś citam utpatiṣyan vicikṣepa pakṣirāja ivoragam
english: About to leap, he flung his tail — round and covered with hair from base to tip — like the king of birds flinging a serpent.

sanskrit: tasya lāṅgūlam āviddham ativegasya pṛṣṭhataḥ dadṛśe garuḍeneva hriyamāṇo mahoragaḥ
english: His tail, whirling behind him as he sped at great velocity, looked like a great serpent being carried off by Garuḍa.

sanskrit: bāhū saṃstambhayām āsa mahāparighasaṃnibhau sasāda ca kapiḥ kaṭyāṃ caraṇau saṃcukopa ca
english: He braced his arms, which resembled great iron bars; the monkey crouched at the haunches and tensed his feet.

sanskrit: saṃhṛtya ca bhujau śrīmāṃs tathaiva ca śirodharām tejaḥ sattvaṃ tathā vīryam āviveśa sa vīryavān
english: Drawing in his arms and likewise his neck, the glorious and valiant one channeled into himself his brilliance, vitality, and heroic energy.

sanskrit: mārgam ālokayan dūrād ūrdhvapraṇihitekṣaṇaḥ rurodha hṛdaye prāṇān ākāśam avalokayan
english: Gazing far ahead at the path, his eyes directed upward, gazing at the sky, he held the breath in his heart.

sanskrit: padbhyāṃ dṛḍham avasthānaṃ kṛtvā sa kapikuñjaraḥ nikuñcya karṇau hanumān utpatiṣyan mahābalaḥ vānarān vānaraśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having planted his feet firmly, and drawing in his ears, the mighty Hanūmān — foremost elephant among monkeys, about to spring — spoke these words to the monkeys, the best of monkeys:

sanskrit: yathā rāghavanirmuktaḥ śaraḥ śvasanavikramaḥ gacchet tadvad gamiṣyāmi laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām
english: "As an arrow released by Rāghava, with the force of the wind, would fly, so shall I fly to Laṅkā ruled by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: na hi drakṣyāmi yadi tāṃ laṅkāyāṃ janakātmajām anenaiva hi vegena gamiṣyāmi surālayam
english: If I do not find Janaka's daughter in Laṅkā, I shall go with the same speed to the abode of the gods.

sanskrit: yadi vā tridive sītāṃ na drakṣyāmi kṛtaśramaḥ baddhvā rākṣasarājānam ānayiṣyāmi rāvaṇam
english: Or if I do not find Sītā in the triple heaven after all my efforts, I shall bind the king of the Rākṣasas and bring Rāvaṇa back.

sanskrit: sarvathā kṛtakāryo 'ham eṣyāmi saha sītayā ānayiṣyāmi vā laṅkāṃ samutpāṭya sarāvaṇām
english: In any case I shall return having accomplished my mission — either with Sītā, or I shall uproot Laṅkā together with Rāvaṇa and bring it here."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu hanumān vānarān vānarottamaḥ utpapātātha vegena vegavān avicārayan
english: Having spoken thus to the monkeys, Hanūmān, foremost among monkeys and swift of movement, then leapt forth with great speed, without hesitation.

sanskrit: samutpatati tasmiṃs tu vegāt te nagarohiṇaḥ saṃhṛtya viṭapān sarvān samutpetuḥ samantataḥ
english: As he leapt upward with speed, the trees that clung to the mountain, drawing in all their branches, sprang up on every side.

sanskrit: sa mattakoyaṣṭibhakān pādapān puṣpaśālinaḥ udvahann ūruvegena jagāma vimale 'mbare
english: Carrying along the flowering trees — including the intoxicated koyaṣṭibhaka — by the force of his thighs, he moved through the clear sky.

sanskrit: ūruvegoddhatā vṛkṣā muhūrtaṃ kapim anvayuḥ prasthitaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ svabandhum iva bāndhavāḥ
english: The trees borne aloft by the force of his thighs followed the monkey for a moment on his long journey, like kinsmen following a dear one setting out.

sanskrit: tam ūruvegonmathitāḥ sālāś cānye nagottamāḥ anujagmur hanūmantaṃ sainyā iva mahīpatim
english: The śāla trees and other foremost trees, churned up by the force of his thighs, followed Hanūmān like soldiers following a king.

sanskrit: supuṣpitāgrair bahubhiḥ pādapair anvitaḥ kapiḥ hanumān parvatākāro babhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ
english: Attended by the many trees with their fully-blossomed tops, the monkey Hanūmān, mountain-like, became wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: sāravanto 'tha ye vṛkṣā nyamajjaṃl lavaṇāmbhasi bhayād iva mahendrasya parvatā varuṇālaye
english: Then the sturdy trees among them sank into the salt water, as if mountains in fear of Mahendra had submerged into the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: sa nānākusumaiḥ kīrṇaḥ kapiḥ sāṅkurakorakaiḥ śuśubhe meghasaṃkāśaḥ khadyotair iva parvataḥ
english: The monkey, strewn with various blossoms together with their sprouts and buds, cloud-like, shone like a mountain lit with fireflies.

sanskrit: vimuktās tasya vegena muktvā puṣpāṇi te drumāḥ avaśīryanta salile nivṛttāḥ suhṛdo yathā
english: Released by his speed, those trees, having shed their blossoms, fell back into the water like friends who have escorted one as far as they can and then returned.

sanskrit: laghutvenopapannaṃ tad vicitraṃ sāgare 'patat drumāṇāṃ vividhaṃ puṣpaṃ kapivāyusamīritam
english: That varied, motley mass of flowers from the trees, stirred by the monkey-wind, fell lightly and beautifully upon the ocean.

sanskrit: puṣpaugheṇānubaddhena nānāvarṇena vānaraḥ babhau megha ivodyan vai vidyudgaṇavibhūṣitaḥ
english: Trailed by the flood of multi-colored blossoms, the monkey shone like a rising cloud adorned with clusters of lightning.

sanskrit: tasya vegasamudbhūtaiḥ puṣpais toyam adṛśyata tārābhir abhirāmābhir uditābhir ivāmbaram
english: The water, scattered with blossoms arising from his speed, looked like the sky adorned with lovely, risen stars.

sanskrit: tasyāmbaragatau bāhū dadṛśāte prasāritau parvatāgrād viniṣkrāntau pañcāsyāv iva pannagau
english: His two arms, stretched out as he moved through the sky, appeared to issue from the mountain's peak like two five-headed serpents.

sanskrit: pibann iva babhau cāpi sormijālaṃ mahārṇavam pipāsur iva cākāśaṃ dadṛśe sa mahākapiḥ
english: He appeared as if drinking the great ocean with its wave-mass, and the great monkey seemed as if thirsting to consume the sky.

sanskrit: tasya vidyutprabhākāre vāyumārgānusāriṇaḥ nayane viprakāśete parvatasthāv ivānalau
english: His two eyes, gleaming with the brilliance of lightning as he sped along the path of the wind, blazed like two fires on a mountain.

sanskrit: piṅge piṅgākṣamukhyasya bṛhatī parimaṇḍale cakṣuṣī saṃprakaśete candrasūryāv iva sthitau
english: The two large, round, tawny eyes of that foremost tawny-eyed one shone like the moon and the sun standing together.

sanskrit: mukhaṃ nāsikayā tasya tāmrayā tāmram ābabhau saṃdhyayā samabhispṛṣṭaṃ yathā sūryasya maṇḍalam
english: His face, reddened by his copper-hued nose, shone like the orb of the sun touched by twilight.

sanskrit: lāṅgalaṃ ca samāviddhaṃ plavamānasya śobhate ambare vāyuputrasya śakradhvaja ivocchritaḥ
english: The tail of Vāyu's son, whirling as he leapt, blazed in the sky like the banner of Śakra raised aloft.

sanskrit: lāṅgūlacakreṇa mahāñ śukladaṃṣṭro 'nilātmajaḥ vyarocata mahāprājñaḥ pariveṣīva bhāskaraḥ
english: The great, white-toothed son of Anila, most wise, shone with the wheel of his curling tail like the sun with its halo.

sanskrit: sphigdeśenābhitāmreṇa rarāja sa mahākapiḥ mahatā dāriteneva girir gairikadhātunā
english: The great monkey, with his copper-red haunches, blazed like a mountain with a great vein of red ochre exposed.

sanskrit: tasya vānarasiṃhasya plavamānasya sāgaram kakṣāntaragato vāyur jīmūta iva garjati
english: As this lion among monkeys leapt across the ocean, the wind trapped in his armpits roared like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: khe yathā nipataty ulkā uttarāntād viniḥsṛtā dṛśyate sānubandhā ca tathā sa kapikuñjaraḥ
english: As a meteor issuing from the northern end falls and is seen trailing its wake through the sky, so was that elephant among monkeys.

sanskrit: patatpataṃgasaṃkāśo vyāyataḥ śuśubhe kapiḥ pravṛddha iva mātaṃgaḥ kakṣyayā badhyamānayā
english: Resembling a flying bird in his darting motion, the extended monkey shone like a great elephant being girthed with a belly-band.

sanskrit: upariṣṭāc charīreṇa chāyayā cāvagāḍhayā sāgare mārutāviṣṭā naur ivāsīt tadā kapiḥ
english: With his body above and his deep shadow below on the ocean, the monkey was then like a boat wind-driven upon the sea.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ deśaṃ samudrasya jagāma sa mahākapiḥ sa sa tasyāṅgavegena sonmāda iva lakṣyate
english: Whatever region of the ocean the great monkey traversed, that region appeared as if agitated to frenzy by the force of his body.

sanskrit: sāgarasyormijālānām urasā śailavarṣmaṇām abhighnaṃs tu mahāvegaḥ pupluve sa mahākapiḥ
english: Striking with his chest the wave-masses of the ocean that were mountain-high, the great monkey sped across at tremendous velocity.

sanskrit: kapivātaś ca balavān meghavātaś ca niḥsṛtaḥ sāgaraṃ bhīmanirghoṣaṃ kampayām āsatur bhṛśam
english: The powerful wind created by the monkey and the wind issuing from the clouds greatly shook the ocean with its terrible roar.

sanskrit: vikarṣann ūrmijālāni bṛhanti lavaṇāmbhasi atyakrāman mahāvegas taraṅgān gaṇayann iva
english: Dragging the great wave-masses in the salt sea, he surpassed them at great speed, as if counting the waves as he went.

sanskrit: plavamānaṃ samīkṣyātha bhujaṅgāḥ sāgarālayāḥ vyomni taṃ kapiśārdūlaṃ suparṇam iti menire
english: Seeing that tiger among monkeys leaping through the sky, the serpents dwelling in the ocean took him for Suparṇa — Garuḍa.

sanskrit: daśayojanavistīrṇā triṃśadyojanam āyatā chāyā vānarasiṃhasya jale cārutarābhavat
english: The shadow of that lion among monkeys, ten leagues wide and thirty leagues long, became most beautiful upon the waters.

sanskrit: śvetābhraghanarājīva vāyuputrānugāminī tasya sā śuśubhe chāyā vitatā lavaṇāmbhasi
english: His shadow, spread out upon the salt water and following in the wake of Vāyu's son, shone like a dense bank of white clouds.

sanskrit: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā plavagaṃ tvaritaṃ tadā vavṛṣuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi devagandharvadānavāḥ
english: Seeing that monkey leaping swiftly then, the gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas rained down showers of flowers.

sanskrit: tatāpa na hi taṃ sūryaḥ plavantaṃ vānareśvaram siṣeve ca tadā vāyū rāmakāryārthasiddhaye
english: The sun did not scorch that lord of monkeys as he leapt; and the wind attended upon him for the accomplishment of Rāma's purpose.

sanskrit: ṛṣayas tuṣṭuvuś cainaṃ plavamānaṃ vihāyasā jaguś ca devagandharvāḥ praśaṃsanto mahaujasaṃ
english: The sages praised him as he flew through the heavens, and gods and Gandharvas sang, extolling him of mighty splendor.

sanskrit: nāgāś ca tuṣṭuvur yakṣā rakṣāṃsi vibudhāḥ khagāḥ prekṣyākāśe kapivaraṃ sahasā vigataklamam
english: Nāgas and Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, gods, and birds praised him, suddenly seeing the foremost monkey flying through the sky, free from fatigue.

sanskrit: tasmin plavagaśārdūle plavamāne hanūmati ikṣvākukulamānārthī cintayām āsa sāgaraḥ
english: While that tiger among monkeys, Hanūmān, was leaping, the ocean, concerned for the honor of the Ikṣvāku lineage, pondered.

sanskrit: sāhāyyaṃ vānarendrasya yadi nāhaṃ hanūmataḥ kariṣyāmi bhaviṣyāmi sarvavācyo vivakṣatām
english: "If I do not render assistance to Hanūmān, that king among monkeys, I shall become the subject of reproach from all those who wish to speak.

sanskrit: aham ikṣvākunāthena sagareṇa vivardhitaḥ ikṣvākusacivaś cāyaṃ nāvasīditum arhati
english: I was enlarged by Sagara, lord of the Ikṣvākus; and this one serves the Ikṣvākus — he ought not to sink in exhaustion.

sanskrit: tathā mayā vidhātavyaṃ viśrameta yathā kapiḥ śeṣaṃ ca mayi viśrāntaḥ sukhenātipatiṣyati
english: I must arrange matters so that the monkey may rest; and having rested upon me, he shall fly the remainder of the way with ease."

sanskrit: iti kṛtvā matiṃ sādhvīṃ samudraś channam ambhasi hiraṇyanābhaṃ mainākam uvāca girisattamam
english: Having made this wholesome resolve, the ocean spoke to Maināka of the golden peak, that foremost of mountains, which was submerged in the water.

sanskrit: tvam ihāsurasaṃghānāṃ pātālatalavāsinām devarājñā giriśreṣṭha parighaḥ saṃniveśitaḥ
english: "O foremost of mountains, you were placed here as a bolt-lock by the king of the gods against the hordes of Asuras dwelling in the floor of Pātāla.

sanskrit: tvam eṣāṃ jñātavīryāṇāṃ punar evotpatiṣyatām pātālasyāprameyasya dvāram āvṛtya tiṣṭhasi
english: You stand blocking the door to the unfathomable Pātāla, preventing those whose strength is known from flying up again.

sanskrit: tiryag ūrdhvam adhaś caiva śaktis te śailavardhitum tasmāt saṃcodayāmi tvām uttiṣṭha nagasattama
english: You have the power to grow sideways, upward, and downward; therefore I urge you — rise up, O best of mountains.

sanskrit: sa eṣa kapiśārdūlas tvām uparyeti vīryavān hanūmān rāmakāryārthaṃ bhīmakarmā kham āplutaḥ
english: This tiger among monkeys, the valiant and terrible-in-deed Hanūmān, who has leapt into the sky for the purpose of Rāma's mission, passes over you.

sanskrit: tasya sāhyaṃ mayā kāryam ikṣvākukulavartinaḥ mama ikṣvākavaḥ pūjyāḥ paraṃ pūjyatamās tava
english: I must render assistance to him who acts for the Ikṣvāku line. The Ikṣvākus are revered by me, but supremely revered by you.

sanskrit: kuru sācivyam asmākaṃ na naḥ kāryam atikramet kartavyam akṛtaṃ kāryaṃ satāṃ manyum udīrayet
english: Render us this service; let not our duty go unperformed. A task that ought to be done but is left undone would rouse the indignation of the good.

sanskrit: salilād ūrdhvam uttiṣṭha tiṣṭhatv eṣa kapis tvayi asmākam atithiś caiva pūjyaś ca plavatāṃ varaḥ
english: Rise up from the water, let this monkey stand upon you; he is both our guest and worthy of honor — the foremost of those who leap.

sanskrit: cāmīkaramahānābha devagandharvasevita hanūmāṃs tvayi viśrāntas tataḥ śeṣaṃ gamiṣyati
english: O Maināka of the great golden peak, attended upon by gods and Gandharvas, once Hanūmān has rested upon you he shall then proceed for the remainder of the way."

sanskrit: kākutsthasyānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca maithilyāś ca vivāsanam śramaṃ ca plavagendrasya samīkṣyotthātum arhasi
english: Considering the gentleness of Kākutstha, the banishment of Maithilī, and the exertion of the lord of leaping monkeys, you ought to rise up.

sanskrit: hiraṇyanābho maināko niśamya lavaṇāmbhasaḥ utpapāta jalāt tūrṇaṃ mahādrumalatāyutaḥ
english: Golden-peaked Maināka, hearing this from the salt sea, quickly sprang up from the water, together with great trees and creepers.

sanskrit: sa sāgarajalaṃ bhittvā babhūvātyutthitas tadā yathā jaladharaṃ bhittvā dīptaraśmir divākaraḥ
english: He rose exceedingly high, bursting through the sea's water, as the sun with blazing rays bursts through a cloud.

sanskrit: śātakumbhamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ sakiṃnaramahoragaiḥ ādityodayasaṃkāśair ālikhadbhir ivāmbaram
english: With his golden peaks inhabited by Kiṃnaras and great serpents, gleaming like the sunrise, seemingly scratching the sky,

sanskrit: tasya jāmbūnadaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ parvatasya samutthitaiḥ ākāśaṃ śastrasaṃkāśam abhavat kāñcanaprabham
english: as the mountain's golden peaks rose up, the sky became resplendent, gleaming like a golden weapon.

sanskrit: jātarūpamayaiḥ śṛṅgair bhrājamānaiḥ svayaṃ prabhaiḥ ādityaśatasaṃkāśaḥ so 'bhavad girisattamaḥ
english: With its peaks of pure gold, self-luminous and blazing, that best of mountains became as resplendent as a hundred suns.

sanskrit: tam utthitam asaṃgena hanūmān agrataḥ sthitam madhye lavaṇatoyasya vighno 'yam iti niścitaḥ
english: Hanūmān, seeing it rise suddenly and stand before him in the middle of the salt water, was certain: "This is an obstacle."

sanskrit: sa tam ucchritam atyarthaṃ mahāvego mahākapiḥ urasā pātayām āsa jīmūtam iva mārutaḥ
english: That great monkey of tremendous speed struck it down with his chest as it stood immensely high — as the wind strikes down a thundercloud.
